verdict.rationale: Better Auth's documented design stores all user data in a database you configure yourself (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and more). Community users confirm it keeps all auth data in your own DB with no tie to a DB provider, so where data lives is entirely your choice. However, the product has no residency or region features of its own; actual region placement depends on wherever you host your database. missing for 10: explicit data-residency/region documentation, first-party region selection or residency guarantees, independent corroboration of residency compliance setups
